name: 360Giving
what: 360Giving is a charity that helps grantmakers publish and use open data about their funding, so people can see who is funding what and where.

name: Apps for Good
what: Apps for Good provides free creative technology courses that teachers can run in the classroom, aimed at preparing students for a changing world of work.
tags: education; courses; young people; digital skills

name: Big Brother Watch
what: Big Brother Watch campaigns against threats to privacy and civil liberties in the UK, including state surveillance and the collection of personal data.

name: Centre for Public Data
what: The Centre for Public Data works to improve the UK's public data. It campaigns to fill gaps in data collection and to strengthen data provisions in new legislation.

name: Citizens Advice
what: Citizens Advice gives free, independent advice on benefits, debt, housing, employment, and consumer problems. The advice is published on its website and delivered by advisers in local offices across the UK.

name: Code Club
what: Code Club is a global community of free clubs where young people learn programming and digital making. It is part of the Raspberry Pi Foundation and provides projects and training for the volunteers who run clubs.

name: CoTech
what: CoTech is a network of worker-owned technology co-operatives in the UK. Its members build software and digital services, and cooperate on client work and shared infrastructure.

name: Crisis
what: Crisis is a national charity for people experiencing homelessness. It runs services for people who are homeless and campaigns for the policy changes needed to end homelessness.

name: data.gov.uk
what: data.gov.uk is the UK government's home for public data. It brings datasets published by departments and public bodies together in one catalogue that anyone can search and download from.

name: Democracy Club
what: Democracy Club produces election data for the UK. It runs a national polling station finder and a candidate database, and publishes the underlying data for others to reuse.
tags: elections; open data; civic tech; voting

name: Full Fact
what: Full Fact checks claims made online and in the news, and works with platforms, regulators, and researchers to reduce the harm caused by bad information.

name: Good Things Foundation
what: Good Things Foundation is a UK digital inclusion charity. It works with a network of local partners to help people get online, get hold of devices, and build the skills and confidence to use them.
tags: digital inclusion; digital skills; devices; charity

name: Government Digital Service
what: The Government Digital Service is the digital centre of government. It builds and sets standards for UK public services online, including GOV.UK itself.
tags: govtech; public services; standards; digital government

name: Green Web Foundation
what: The Green Web Foundation works towards a fossil-free internet. It runs a check and a hosting directory that show whether a website is served using green energy, and publishes the dataset behind them.

name: Homeless Link
what: Homeless Link is the national membership charity for organisations working directly with people who become homeless in England. It works to improve those services and campaigns for policy change.

name: Liberty
what: Liberty is a UK civil liberties organisation. It campaigns and takes legal cases on rights issues, including those raised by surveillance and the use of personal data.
tags: civil liberties; human rights; litigation; campaigning

name: LocalGov Digital
what: LocalGov Digital is a network for digital practitioners working in and around local government, providing a place for councils to share work on common problems.

name: mySociety
what: mySociety provides technology, research, and data that help people take part in civic life. Its tools, among them FixMyStreet and TheyWorkForYou, are used in more than 40 countries.
tags: civic tech; democracy; research; open source

name: Office for National Statistics
what: The Office for National Statistics is the UK's national statistical institute and its largest independent producer of official statistics. It publishes data on the population, the economy, and society.
tags: official statistics; open data; government; population

name: Open Climate Fix
what: Open Climate Fix builds open forecasting tools, mostly using machine learning, to help electricity grids plan around renewable generation and cut carbon emissions.

name: Open Data Institute
what: The Open Data Institute is a London-based non-profit founded in 2012 by Tim Berners-Lee and Nigel Shadbolt. It researches how data is collected and used, and advises organisations on doing that openly and accountably.
tags: open data; research; policy; data ethics

name: Open Data Manchester
what: Open Data Manchester helps people, organisations, and communities use data better, through advice, advocacy, events, research, and training.
tags: open data; training; community; greater manchester

name: Open Innovations
what: Open Innovations is a not-for-profit in Leeds that works in the open with sponsors and partners to turn open data into tools and evidence for better decisions.

name: Open Rights Group
what: Open Rights Group is a UK campaigning organisation working on digital rights. It focuses on privacy and free speech online, and on how data and technology affect people's rights.
tags: digital rights; privacy; free speech; campaigning

name: OpenSAFELY
what: OpenSAFELY is a platform for analysing large, sensitive datasets safely and securely. It is built by a team at the Bennett Institute so that approved researchers can work with NHS data under tight controls.
tags: health data; research; privacy; open source

name: OpenUK
what: OpenUK is a not-for-profit and the UK body for the business of open technology, covering open source software, open hardware, open data, and open standards.
tags: open source; open standards; open data; advocacy

name: Privacy International
what: Privacy International is a charity based in London that works on the intersection of modern technology and human rights, with a focus on surveillance and the exploitation of personal data.

name: Raspberry Pi Foundation
what: The Raspberry Pi Foundation is a charity with a mission to help young people realise their potential through computing and digital technologies. It publishes free learning resources and supports clubs and teachers.

name: RNIB
what: The Royal National Institute of Blind People supports blind and partially sighted people across the UK. It advises on assistive and accessible technology, and campaigns for accessible products and services.

name: Scope
what: Scope is a disability equality charity in England and Wales. It provides practical information and campaigns on the barriers disabled people face, including in digital services.

name: Shelter England
what: Shelter is a housing and homelessness charity in England. It advises people and families on their housing rights, challenges unfair housing practice, and campaigns for better housing policy.

name: The Restart Project
what: The Restart Project helps people use their electronics for longer, which keeps working devices out of waste. It supports community repair events and campaigns for the right to repair.
tags: right to repair; electronics; waste; community

name: TheyWorkForYou
what: TheyWorkForYou, run by mySociety, makes the UK's parliaments easier to follow. You can look up who represents you and see how they have voted and what they have said in debates.

name: Turn2us
what: Turn2us is a charity that helps people facing financial insecurity. It runs online tools to check benefit entitlement and to search for charitable grants.
